stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist resolved a criminal matter in another state by admitting to sufficient facts, and the case was continued without a finding and later dismissed. She tells the Board she has no conviction to report. How should that resolution be characterised for Board purposes?

choices.text: Not a conviction, because the case was ultimately dismissed by the court.
Not a conviction, because no sentence was ever imposed upon her.
Not a conviction, because the matter arose outside of the Commonwealth.
A conviction only if the Board separately finds that she committed the crime.
A conviction, because an admission to sufficient facts and a continuance without a finding are included.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 10.02 defines conviction to include any admission to or finding of sufficient facts to warrant a finding of guilt, regardless of adjudication, a continuance without a finding, and any plea of guilty or nolo contendere, of or to a crime in any jurisdiction, accepted by the court, whether or not a sentence has been imposed. Each of the features she relies on is expressly inside the definition.

choice_analysis.A: Regardless of adjudication is part of the definition, so a later dismissal does not remove it.
choice_analysis.B: The definition applies whether or not a sentence has been imposed.
choice_analysis.C: The definition reaches a crime in any jurisdiction.
choice_analysis.D: No separate Board finding is needed; the definition applies on its own terms.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: both features named are inside the regulatory definition.

related_facts: A conviction of a person licensed by the Board is conclusive evidence of the commission of that crime in a disciplinary proceeding based upon it.
explanation.mpje_trap: The regulatory definition is broader than the ordinary meaning and expressly covers a continuance without a finding.

reasoning_steps: Read the regulatory definition rather than the ordinary meaning of conviction
Match the admission to sufficient facts and the continuance without a finding to the listed items
Disregard the absence of a sentence and the out-of-state forum
